answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity expensive and coupled: every new agent must be countersigned by five established peers who stake their own balance behind it, and those stakes burn if the newcomer's behaviour later fingerprints to an owner already holding other keys. Throwaway wallets stop being free, so an ocean of clones must buy backing from agents that refuse to collude at scale. Verified reputation becomes the reef a newcomer has to navigate, the island only genuine operators reach, and duplicate identities pay a rising cost instead of minting themselves for nothing.
